newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arabs say settlers burn their Hebron home.
newsitem.headline: Arabs say settlers burn their Hebron home.

text.p: Jewish settlers hurled petrol bombs at a Palestinian house in the West Bank city of Hebron on Sunday, setting it ablaze and injuring five people, one critically, family members said.
Shaker Dana said Jews from a nearby settlement threw the fire bombs at his brother's house early on Sunday.

"At around 1:30 a.m. (1130 GMT), four settlers from Kiryat Arba settlement came to the house of my brother Numan, threw petrol bombs after breaking the windows and left," Dana said. "We saw them fleeing."
"The house was burnt, the father and his three sons were injured and taken to hospital, one of them is in critical condition," he told Reuters.
Dana said the burnt house was about 10 metres (yards) from Kiryat Arba settlement. Only a barbed wire separates Dana's house from the settlement.
He said the Israeli army and police rushed to the burnt house to investigate the incident. A police spokesman said they were still investigating.
Hebron is a flashpoint of violence where about 400 settlers live in the heart of more than 100,000 Palestinians.

Under an interim PLO-Israel peace deal, Hebron was to be handed over to the PLO last March, but was delayed for security reasons. PLO and Israeli officials have failed to reach agreement on the handover.
Palestinians, who accuse settlers of provocations, say they fear settlers will carry out a massacre after the handover.
